changes.before: Complete repeat_text(text, /, count=2): return text repeated count times. text must remain positional-only; count may be passed by position or keyword. Inputs are text and a nonnegative integer.
changes.after: Learn how a slash makes text positional-only while count can be passed by position or keyword.

before: A slash / in a parameter list marks preceding parameters as positional-only. A caller must supply those values by position, not by writing their parameter names.

Parameters between / and * can be passed by position or name. Parameters after a bare * are keyword-only. These markers describe allowed calls, not the types of values. Multiplying a string by a nonnegative integer repeats its text that many times; a zero count produces empty text.
Positional-only parameters can prevent callers from depending on internal parameter names. They are an API-design choice, not required for every function.

The supplied helper beginning with __ is test infrastructure. It calls your function to check the stated input-preservation or allowed-call contract. Leave that helper unchanged; complete only the named task function.
label takes positional text and an optional named prefix. Returns concatenated text; positional-only text cannot be supplied by name.

```python
def label(text, /, *, prefix="Note: "):
    return prefix + text

print(label("Moon", prefix="Topic: "))
```
This prints:
```text
Topic: Moon
```
